note: The screen captures the video uses, in sets: each set is one screen rectangle at one Windows scale, so the video swaps its pictures in place and only the drawn layers move (docs/research/promo-video.md, 'Real captures and drawn parts'). w and h are the rectangle in capture pixels; boxes and rows are places inside it in the same pixels (the cursor, the ring and the pops land on them). No capture yet: file null and standIn true, and the draft draws a plain sketch of the set with a stand-in tag; boxes and rows are then the sketch's own. The capture session (p6-media Part B) puts each file under public/shots/, sets file, standIn false and from, sets w, h and scale to the capture, and measures boxes and rows from the pictures. The final render refuses a shot with no file or standIn true.

tray.what: the tray icon and the space above it, where its tooltip shows (one fixed rectangle at 200% on the DELL screen)

S3.what: holding tooltip of a real Claude Code session

S5b.what: Keep awake hovered, its submenu open
